thesis: This is a four-session week that ends on Friday's August CPI print: the 10Y has closed a full week above its 4.75% stress line (4.78%), September hike odds sit near 60%, WTI is back at $91 on renewed Hormuz strikes, and VIX at 14.5 with narrow breadth trips the Council's own rule to size down in a complacent market. We hold 30% cash, in line with Ophelia's 25-30% prescription for the run-up to the print. The rest goes into holdings that react differently to the CPI result: low-volatility healthcare leaders with positive drift (GILD, MDT), energy as the oil and inflation hedge (CVX), a money-center bank that gains from higher-for-longer rates (WFC), and one AI-compute name (NVDA) to take part if CPI cools. No holding reports earnings inside the window (the ORCL and ADBE reports on Thursday are skipped), the book holds no rate-sensitive REITs, utilities or consumer discretionary names, and every position has a price level that voids it (XLV $169.71, XLE $63.46, XLF $57.48, SMH $545.22).
risks: A hot core CPI (0.3% or more month over month) that sends the 10Y through 4.85%, or an unwind of the yen carry trade, would hit NVDA and WFC hardest, while a cool print plus a Hormuz de-escalation would pull money out of energy and defensives and leave the 30% cash lagging SPY. These dates fall after my training data, so I have no memory of how the week went and none was used.
